strings: Proving Your Worth is a crucial step in Sven Yorgen's campaign for revenge in western Duskwood. Before allowing an adventurer to confront the necromancer Morbent Fel directly, the grieving hermit demands proof that they can overcome the undead legions infesting Raven Hill Cemetery.

Sven Yorgen hides in a secluded camp north of the howling woods, consumed by grief and fury over the slaughter of his family. He has pieced together that the shadowy Dark Riders who razed his homestead were allied with a sinister necromancer named Morbent Fel. Though Sven hungers for retribution, he is not reckless enough to throw an untried recruit directly into Fel's grasp. He demands a display of sheer combat mastery against the skeletal forces occupying Raven Hill Cemetery.

To satisfy Sven, adventurers must push deep into the necropolis of Raven Hill, south of Forlorn Rowe. The mausoleum and the surrounding grounds crawl with restless corpses bound by Fel's foul magic: sword-wielding Skeletal Raiders patrol the tombstones, while Skeletal Warders and Healers tend the darker chambers beneath the earth. Clearing this vanguard is a bloody chore, especially with horrors like the vengeful phantom Mor'Ladim prowling the cemetery paths.

Surviving the bone-strewn catacombs convinces Sven that his ally possesses more than just empty courage. However, defeating Fel's lesser minions is only the prelude. Morbent Fel wields dark protective enchantments that render him nearly untouchable by mundane arms, forcing Sven to seek greater wisdom and ancient relics before the final confrontation can begin.
Why does Sven make me fight skeletons before facing Morbent Fel?

Sven knows Morbent Fel is a lethal necromancer allied with the mysterious Dark Riders. He refuses to send an ally to a meaningless death until they demonstrate the stamina and tactical skill needed to cut through an entire vanguard of undead minions.
why proving your worth | why sven makes me kill skeletons | sven test

While Skeletal Raiders wander the open cemetery grounds south of Forlorn Rowe, Skeletal Healers and Warders are primarily found concentrated inside and immediately around the large mausoleum and crypt tunnels west of the cemetery's center.
where are warders | where are skeletal healers | find skeletal warders
Who is Mor'Ladim and why should I watch out for him here?

Mor'Ladim is a powerful, tragic undead knight who roams the paths of Raven Hill Cemetery. He is far stronger than the ordinary skeletons around the crypts and will quickly cut down unwary adventurers.
morladim danger | who is mor'ladim | wandering elite raven hill
How is Morbent Fel connected to the Dark Riders?

Sven discovered that Morbent Fel allied with the cloaked Dark Riders who butchered his wife and children. While the riders vanished back into the shadows, Fel remains anchored in Duskwood, continuing his foul necromancy.
morbent fel dark riders connection | why dark riders and fel | sven family killers
What happens after completing this quest?

Once you prove your combat prowess, Sven acknowledges your strength but explains that Morbent Fel cannot be killed by brute force alone. He directs you to seek counsel from Bishop Farthing in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light to find a way to strip the necromancer of his unholy protections.
next quest after proving your worth | what to do after skeletons

Cleansing Raven Hill Cemetery of Morbent Fel's restless dead is holy work, answering the unburied cries of Duskwood's deceased with the Light's justice.
The desecration of Raven Hill's tombs by dark rituals cries out for spiritual cleansing, putting an end to the warders and healers who pervert life and death.
Western Duskwood has fallen into anarchy without regular Stormwind patrols, leaving devastated frontiersmen like Sven to rely entirely on traveling champions to push back the undead scourge.
Who are the skeletal minions at Raven Hill?

The skeletal raiders, healers, and warders haunting Raven Hill Cemetery are the reanimated dead raised by the necromancer Morbent Fel. Drawn from the desecrated graves of Duskwood, these restless dead now form an unholy bulwark guarding the cemetery crypts and carrying out the dark will of their master.

Sven Yorgen is an isolated hermit surviving alone in the haunted wilderness of Duskwood. Shattered by grief and driven by hatred for the Dark Riders who slaughtered his family, he lacks the strength and resources to assault Morbent Fel's undead army alone. He turns to capable adventurers willing to brave Raven Hill Cemetery to exact his vengeance.

The Lost Ingots is an Alliance task in the Wetlands to recover consecrated metal from a shipwreck. After finding only a single bar in a sunken chest, travelers must hunt down the local Bluegill murlocs who looted the remaining shipment.

Off the misty shores of the Wetlands lies the shattered wreckage of the Flying Osprey. Sent to retrieve precious Lightforge iron for the dwarven priest Glorin Steelbrow, seekers discovered that the cargo hold's waterlogged chest was nearly empty. The ravenous local Bluegill murlocs had already scavenged the rest of the vessel, taking the gleaming ingots for themselves.

Lightforge iron is no ordinary ore; it is rare, specialized metal attuned to work sacred smithing craft. Allowing it to rot in murloc encampments is unthinkable for a dwarf of the Light. By hunting down the Bluegill raiders swarming the shallows near the broken hull, adventurers prise back the scattered bars so Glorin Steelbrow can see the iron hammered into a weapon.

The cargo arrived aboard the Flying Osprey, an unfortunate vessel that met its demise off the coast of the Wetlands. Its broken timbers now lie partially submerged in the shallows.

Only a single ingot remained locked within the waterlogged chest. The coastal Bluegill murlocs had already pried into the sunken wreckage and scavenged the rest of the shipment to scatter among their coastal raiders.

Every metalworker knows the tragedy of seeing superior stock like Lightforge iron end up as curios in a coastal murloc nest instead of an anvil.
Recovering lost masterwork ore and putting it into the hands of a dwarven priest like Glorin Steelbrow honors the long tradition of dwarven craftsmanship and reclaimers.
You carry Morbent's Bane back to Sven Yorgen, the weapon forged to strip away Morbent Fel's unholy defenses.

Morbent Fel's hold over Raven Hill cemetery resists ordinary steel. Blades shatter or glance off the dark wards around the necromancer. A weapon made to break those wards is now ready. Grimand Elmore shaped the metal in Stormwind's Dwarven District, and sacred power consecrated it. Morbent's Bane can now sever Fel's tie to unlife.

Sven Yorgen waits at his lonely camp near Duskwood's western border, after the encroaching darkness brought ruin to his family, farm, and companions. You bring him Morbent's Bane, forged to break Morbent Fel's wards. Sven recognizes the weapon's divine craftsmanship and the fire in your eyes. With the weapon delivered, you can strike at the master of Raven Hill.
Morbent's Bane is a weapon forged and consecrated to break the magical wards surrounding Morbent Fel at Raven Hill.

In the southern Barrens, seasoned Horde hunters seek guidance from Jorn Skyseer. After you hunt local raptors for Sergra Darkthorn, she sends you south to Camp Taurajo, where an elder tracker offers deeper lessons.

You have hunted the cunning sunscale and scytheclaw raptors stalking the northern savannah, earning Sergra Darkthorn's respect at the Crossroads. She knows martial skill must be joined with understanding of the land's great beasts. With her mentorship complete, she sends you south.

Follow the Gold Road south through increasingly rugged plains to Camp Taurajo, a vital tauren settlement near the southern wilds. Jorn Skyseer waits there, an elder tracker ready to teach hunters how to pursue elusive, legendary quarry across the Barrens.

After you hunt the local scytheclaws, Sergra Darkthorn, the raptor hunter at the Crossroads, sends you south. Your hunts prove your tracking and hunting prowess.

Tucked away in the binding of Bookie Herod's ledgers is a small brass key alongside notes referencing a secure strongbox. Locating this container deep within the cavern complex behind Kurzen's Compound may reveal how Private Thorsen was betrayed.

Searching through Bookie Herod's ledgers yields no direct mention of Private Thorsen, but it reveals something else: a small brass key concealed inside a book's binding. Scraps among the paperwork make passing mention of a secure strongbox tucked away inside the Stockpile, the cavern complex at the rear of Kurzen's Compound. Opening that container might reveal how Thorsen's cover was blown.
Reaching the strongbox requires delving into the cave system behind the compound. Heavy, bronze-bound, and sturdily constructed, the chest sits among stacked crates in the cave.

Gazrog at the Crossroads sends you after payroll silver stolen by raptors. Rumors of their cunning lead you south of Ratchet, into the Raptor Grounds. The garrison needs its wages back.

Gazrog needs the Crossroads guards paid, and the raptors have taken their wages. You are sent to recover the stolen coin, not simply punish the beasts. When raptors ambushed the payroll shipment, Gazrog first sought vengeance. But killing the pack would not restore the missing money. The Horde must learn how the raptors carried off heavy crates of coin, and where they took them.

Scouts found a raptor nest between two craggy peaks, south of Ratchet and northwest of Northwatch Hold. The creatures dragged the intact lockbox into their territory, where they guard it alongside eggs and fresh kills. Tales of raptor cunning and hoarding now seem true to Gazrog. Ordinary beasts rarely stash metallic valuables.
Why did raptors steal silver in the first place?

Barrens raptors show startling cunning and curious scavenging habits. They dragged the intact strongbox to their communal nests in the Raptor Grounds, perhaps drawn by its shine, the treated leather on the chest, or a hoarding instinct.

gazrog | who gives stolen silver | crossroads questgiver gazrog

No. Northwatch Hold lies southeast of the Raptor Grounds, but native raptors carried out the theft. Their thievery and hoarding surprised even veteran Horde commanders.

As a member of the Horde, you know the Crossroads keeps its guards paid and fed to hold the Kalimdor frontier.

The area is teeming with fierce Sunscale raptors, surprisingly cunning beasts known to hoard shiny valuables in their nests and aggressively defend the stolen lockbox from any intruders.

Inside Bookie Herod's strongbox lies a damp piece of parchment detailing the daily routines of Private Thorsen. Bearing only the initial M, this correspondence suggests an informant has embedded themselves among the rebels in northern Stranglethorn Vale. The muddy note is meant for Lieutenant Doren.

Opening the strongbox reveals not just valuables, but an itinerary tracking Private Thorsen. The barely legible writing recounts his patrol routes, his companions, and his daily activities around the Rebel Camp, marked only with the signature -M. Such detailed observations could only come from someone living alongside Thorsen, pointing to a traitor within the rebel camp.

Carrying the damp parchment back to the Rebel Camp brings the truth to Lieutenant Doren. Armed with the initialed note, the commander gains the evidence required to search for the infiltrator working within their own perimeter.
What is written on the muddy note?

The note contains an itinerary of Private Thorsen's daily routines. It outlines where he patrols, the people he speaks to, and how he occupies his hours within the camp, closed out by the single letter -M.

Eagan Peltskinner asks you to hunt wolves prowling Northshire Valley and bring him their meat. He waits outside Northshire Abbey, where the valley’s needs continue despite the guards’ focus on Defias bandits.

Eagan Peltskinner waits by Northshire Abbey’s walls with a grudge against the local timber wolves. Marshal McBride and the Stormwind guards have limited strength to defend the abbey from Defias bandits, while tradesfolk still have daily needs. Eagan asks you to thin the wolves’ numbers and bring back their tough meat for his cooking.

Wolves roam closer to Northshire Abbey as patrols weaken. The Kingdom of Stormwind has too few troops and is strained by missing leadership. Young wolves and timber wolves now prowl the abbey’s paths and orchards. Hunting them supplies Eagan’s pantry and makes nearby trails safer for novitiates, laborers, and newly arrived defenders.
Eagan Peltskinner is a hunter and tradesman near the entrance to Northshire Abbey. He dislikes the local timber wolves and is happy to cook and eat their meat.

Young wolves and timber wolves naturally prowl the forested borders and open meadows of Northshire Valley. However, with local Stormwind guards preoccupied by the rising threat of the Defias Brotherhood, the predators roam closer to the abbey grounds unchecked.

Following the discovery of an incriminating message signed only by an initial, Lieutenant Doren seeks to identify the traitor within the Rebel Camp. By cross-referencing duty rosters, duty records can reveal who shared patrol routes with Private Thorsen during the previous week.

The recovered note bears only the initial M, which provides little on its own to expose the conspirator aiding the Kurzen forces. However, the author mentions sharing regular duty paths alongside Private Thorsen throughout the previous week. Lieutenant Doren directs you across the Rebel Camp to speak with Corporal Sethman, the soldier responsible for maintaining duty logs, to identify who walked alongside Thorsen.

Reviewing the official records confirms that Private Merle was assigned to the exact same duty times and routes as Thorsen for the entirety of the prior week. The realization exposes Merle as the informant feeding intelligence to Kurzen's men. Once identified, the traitor flees the encampment toward the northern boundary with Duskwood.
Why does Lieutenant Doren send you to Corporal Sethman?

Corporal Sethman oversees the duty logs and schedules for the Rebel Camp. Because the recovered note mentions walking regular routes with Private Thorsen, Sethman's records can pinpoint who was assigned to duty alongside him.

You carry a snapjaw shell from the Barrens across the sea to Mura Runetotem in Silverpine Forest. Its strange vitality may help the tauren healer aid the Forsaken.

Tonga Runetotem notices something peculiar about altered snapjaws while investigating the magically changed wildlife around the Barrens oases. Their shells pulse with resilient energy despite their corruption. He asks you to carry one across the Great Sea to his clanmate, Mura Runetotem, who is stationed in the Eastern Kingdoms.

Mura Runetotem is at the Sepulcher, a Forsaken outpost in Silverpine Forest. She made the arduous journey there to help the Horde's newest allies cleanse and renew their ailing, blighted woodland. Mura hopes the shell's inner glow and enduring spark of life will reveal ways to restore vitality to the northern continent.
Mura Runetotem is a tauren druid and Tonga Runetotem's clanmate. She traveled across the sea and established herself at the Sepulcher to aid the Forsaken by studying ways to heal their dying forest.

Tauren hold a sacred duty to nurture and mend the natural world. Mura sees that Silverpine Forest is decaying and blighted, and hopes to use the earth's healing traditions to aid the Horde's new allies and restore balance to the soil.

Goblin Engineering is a specialized craft path for master inventors who seek total mastery over explosive power and volatile concussive ordnance. Driven by high-yield blasting powders and relentless firepower, it offers an unapologetically destructive alternative to intricate tinkering.

Engineering in Azeroth divides cleanly into two distinct philosophies, and the goblin school of thought revolves almost entirely around violent combustion. Where other inventors craft delicate clockwork mechanisms or subtle contrivances, goblin tinkerers harness the volatile power of blasting powder to forge tools of staggering devastation. To enter the ranks of goblin engineering is to embrace fire, shrapnel, and concussive force as the ultimate solutions to practical problems.

The goblin engineering tradition does not disguise its hazards. Practitioners pride themselves on maximizing yield and raw destructive potential, welcoming any brave engineer who values decisive firepower over fragile safety regulations.
